It adds the required Upload signature and reuses multipartbody.NewFile, while B changes the required API, adds explicitly forbidden association machinery, and refactors unrelated retry behavior.","reasons":["A provides the exact required signature: Upload(ctx context.Context, fileName string, content io.Reader, opts ...FilesOption). B instead accepts ...UploadFileOption, breaking the frozen API contract.","A uses internal/multipartbody.NewFile with field \"file\" and preserves existing FilesOption handling in its shared add path.","B adds association fields, WithFileFormField, new option interfaces, and NewFileWithFields despite the contract explicitly forbidding association fields and requiring unchanged FilesOption behavior.","B duplicates Add's request construction and response decoding inside Upload instead of routing through Add, then also changes global seekable-body behavior affecting Files.Update and other raw requests—well beyond scope. A at least centralizes those mechanics in one private path shared by Add and Upload."],"risks_a":["A changes Add by eagerly buffering every supplied body, contrary to the requirement to preserve its existing behavior.","A calls the private add helper rather than routing Upload through the public Add method as explicitly required.","The visible tests do not cover empty-filename validation, nil content, or source-reader failures."],"risks_b":["Upload has the wrong public option type and therefore does not implement the exact required convenience API.","It introduces explicitly prohibited association APIs and substantial option-system churn.","It changes generic request/retry, closing, and Content-Length semantics for seekable readers, expanding risk beyond file uploads; its GetBody closure also reuses one mutable seeker across attempts and is unsafe for concurrent body acquisition/use patterns inherent to general transport machinery downgrade/redirect scenarios besides serial retries? More simply shared mutable seeker can be fragile under redirects/retries. But avoid uncertain. Plus comments claim failed SeekEnd leaves offset untouched, not generally guaranteed. Mention concrete. Also no source-reader failure test despite requirements. Good." ]}
